mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase equity valuations.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level as a predictor of 20-day returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month year-over-year increase in the CPIAUCSL index above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where CPIAUCSL 12-month growth exceeds 3.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a robust labor market, which drives consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between UNRATE and PAYEMS is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.5%), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to expected monetary tightening.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.5%), the FEDFUNDS signal fails to predict negative returns (i.e., positive returns occur in more than 50% of triggered instances) or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) level below 900.0 thousand units signals a contraction in the residential sector, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 900.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (2017=100) signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings growth and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (characterized by FEDFUNDS rising above 2.5% and sustained for 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and rising for 3 months), the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high GDP growth rate (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 2.0%) combined with low inflation (CPIAUCSL 12-month growth < 2.0%) indicates a strong economy without inflationary pressure, which supports positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term between GDPC1 growth and CPIAUCSL growth is not significant (p>0.05) in predicting 5-day returns, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.
